prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: A short story of the 2008 financial crisis, from the US housing boom and subprime mortgages to securitization, the fall of Lehman Brothers and the government response. It shows how a chain of risky bets turned a housing bubble into a global crash.

beats.narration: In 2008, a crisis in American home loans nearly brought down the world's banks. It began with a boom. House prices kept climbing, and everyone believed they always would. Lenders grew careless.

clip_queries: for sale sign in front of house

beats.narration: Banks handed subprime mortgages to buyers with weak credit. Then they bundled those loans into securities and sold them to investors worldwide. Risk spread everywhere, and few understood who actually held it.

Then prices stopped rising. Borrowers defaulted, and those securities lost value. Banks that held them were suddenly in danger. Lehman Brothers, a huge investment bank, collapsed, and panic swept through the financial system.
Governments stepped in. The US government rescued banks with public money, and the central bank flooded the system with cash. It stopped the freefall, but millions still lost jobs and homes.

props.heading: The government response
items: Central bank floods system with cash

beats.narration: So what caused it? Easy credit, bundled risk, and a belief that prices could only rise. When trust broke, everything fell. Cheap risk is never really free.

props.text: Cheap risk is never really free.
